Docs/Replay/Guide

Replay

Area effects and buff bursts

2 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓

Novas, reaction/lob-impact flashes and grenade blasts now use filled 24-point discs at depth 8, with their existing radius and payload RGB. Nova base alpha is 0.5; reaction/blast base alpha is 0.45. Over the displayed flash lifetime they expand from 0.92 to 1.06 times the radius while fading to zero. Late observations start partway through that curve, and expiration/correction removes the view.

The original uses a 0.28-second local announcement clock. Replay retains its existing 17-tick flash lifetime (about 0.283 seconds at 60 Hz), deriving progress from displayed state. Nova and reaction discs use observed state; grenade blasts retain predicted local / observed remote selection. Separate bounded banks keep those worlds' lifetimes independent. This is presentation metadata only: the simulation's flash, action/event, content and checkpoint formats are unchanged.

Standing zones are filled 24-point discs, radius from their catalog row and alpha 0.22. Payload RGB is used when its tint is visible; otherwise the original ember fallback applies. They keep their scale, position and alpha until the simulated zone expires. The effective depth is 2, matching the original zone parent's depth 1 plus its disc child's depth 1. Late join and migration display an existing zone without a separate launch event.

Buffs emit the original warm 12-particle, 0.4-second burst at the wearer recorded in the cast flash. A forward-observation tracker produces it once per new cast; initial observations, epoch/run/floor replacement and rewind/replay stay silent. It retains its highest observed tick so rewinding cannot replay an old burst. Existing view-reset/floor/epoch cleanup retires the particles. A flash entirely missed between displayed observations produces no invented historical burst. The existing bounded feedback pool owns and retires the emitter.

Shell
nix develop --command bash examples/replay_scrapyard/area_view_run.sh
REPLAY_PREBUILT=1 RSY_HEADED_HOST=1 RSY_AUDIO_DRIVER=Dummy \
  RSY_AREA_CAPTURE=/absolute/existing/output/directory \
  GODOT=/path/to/Godot bash examples/replay_scrapyard/area_view_run.sh

The native fixture checks nova radius/color/expansion/fade, a zone's constant fill through its last ticks and removal, and buff wearer/particle configuration, single emission and cleanup, plus the disc from a slime landing. Browser acceptance records the corresponding nodes on all three peers. Migration checks the restored filled zone on the promoted host, alongside the existing restored-lob and continued-combat requirements.

Cast paths now cover cone tongues and recorded spread bolts. Remaining impact details, broader devices, audio listening and paired timing/feel evaluation remain work. See evidence and the port ledger.

The renderer now uses immutable ArrayMesh instances for procedural polygons. Color/alpha use instance self modulation; arcs reuse one unit polygon and an affine basis that preserves the existing kink, width and recorded endpoints. Node pools, visibility, lifetimes and simulation formats remain unchanged. This avoids the stock web renderer's Polygon2D index-update path, including during viewport resize. See the rendering audit.
